attributes.body_ja:
「なんか」は、副助詞（ふくじょし）の「など」に関連（かんれん）した表現（ひょうげん）です。多（おお）くの場合（ばあい）、この二（ふた）つは同（おな）じような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。「なんか」も副助詞（ふくじょし）として扱（あつか）われることもあります。「なんて」はこの「なんか」を発展（はってん）させた形（かたち）で、「などという」を短（みじか）くしたものと考（かんが）えられています。

「なんか」と「なんて」はどちらも、「など」や「のような」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。「なんか」と「なんて」の主（おも）な違（ちが）いは、「なんて」は用言（ようげん）（活用（かつよう）する語（ご）―動詞（どうし）、イ形容詞（けいようし）、ナ形容詞（けいようし））のあとに使（つか）われることが多（おお）いのに対（たい）して、「なんか」は体言（たいげん）（活用（かつよう）しない語（ご）―名詞（めいし））のあとに使（つか）われることがほとんどであることです。

ただし、この使（つか）い分（わ）けはそれほど厳（きび）しくありません。ほとんどの母語話者（ぼごわしゃ）は「なんか」と「なんて」を体言（たいげん）に付（つ）けても用言（ようげん）に付（つ）けても間違（まちが）っているとは感（かん）じないでしょう。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「なんか」と「なんて」は、そのあとに続（つづ）く言葉（ことば）を低（ひく）く評価（ひょうか）するニュアンスを持（も）つことがあります。そのため、自分（じぶん）に使（つか）えば謙遜（けんそん）になり、他人（たにん）に使（つか）えば悪口（わるぐち）のように聞（き）こえる可能性（かのうせい）があります。

ただし、現代（げんだい）では会話（かいわ）の間（ま）を埋（う）めるために使（つか）われることも多（おお）いので、あまり気（き）にしないで使（つか）ってみましょう。
attributes.body:
なんか is an expression in Japanese that is frequently associated with the adverbial particle など. They are thought to have overlapping meanings in many circumstances, and なんか itself may be considered an adverbial particle. なんて is an extension of this, and may be considered an abbreviation of などという 'to say something like'.

Both なんか and なんて are used in the same way as など, having translations like 'such as', and 'things like' in English. The primary difference between なんか and なんて is that なんて is far more common after 用言（ようげん） (conjugatable words). This includes verbs, い-Adjectives, and な-Adjectives. On the other hand, なんか is almost exclusively used after 体言（たいげん） (unconjugatable words). In other words, nouns.

Despite the 体言（たいげん） and 用言（ようげん） tendency, most native speakers will not consider it incorrect to use either なんか or なんて with any type of word.

Fun Fact

Both なんか and なんて are often used to show a low evaluation of the word that they follow. This can come across as humility when used in relation to oneself, or as an insult when used in relation to others.

Don't let this point stop you from using なんか or なんて though, as many native speakers use it simply to fill the silence in modern Japanese.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese
A Dictionary of Advanced Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: なんて, なんと and なんか - when and how exactly do you use these three?

attributes.body: Both なんか・なんて and など can be used to give examples, like '(A) and so on' or 'things like (A)', but they differ in nuance and formality. など is neutral and used in both speech and writing. なんか・なんて are more casual and often carry a dismissive or belittling tone, like '(A) and whatever' or 'unimportant things like (A)'.

second_relatable.title: など
second_relatable.meaning: Such as, Things like, Etc., And so on

attributes.body: って casually introduces or refers back to a topic, e.g. あの人って優しいよね ('That person is really kind, huh?') なんか・なんて adds a dismissive or emotional tone, often implying downplaying or surprise, e.g. 私なんかにできるかな ('Can someone like me really do it?')

first_relatable.title: って
first_relatable.meaning: As for, Speaking of, Casual は (Sentence topic marker)

attributes.body: なんか・なんて and とか～とか both give examples, but differ in tone and usage. なんか・なんて usually follows a single noun to imply 'things like (A)', often with a dismissive or belittling nuance. とか～とか is used after each item in a list and simply means 'things like (A), (B), and so forth' without any negative implication.

second_relatable.title: とか～とか
second_relatable.meaning: Among other things, For example, Such as

attributes.body: Both add emphasis, but with opposite nuance. なんか・なんて often downplays or dismisses, while こそ highlights importance or exclusivity. The former can feel self-deprecating or casual, while the latter stresses that something uniquely applies. Compare 私なんかできるのかな？ ('I wonder if someone like me could do it?') versus 彼こそできる ('Him, if no one else, can do it.')

second_relatable.title: こそ
second_relatable.meaning: For sure, For certain, Even more so, Underlined or bolded text

attributes.body: Both express that something is one example of a larger group, but differ in usage. といった is neutral and often used to classify or exemplify within a broader group, e.g. 'ピアノやギターといった楽器' ('musical instruments such as the piano and guitar'). なんか・なんて is more casual and implies a dismissive attitude, e.g. '宿題なんかしたくない' ('I don't want to do homework or anything like that').

first_relatable.title: といった
first_relatable.meaning: Such as, Like, So much as

attributes.body: まさか and なんか・なんて are both used to express surprise, but function in different ways. まさか comes at the beginning of a sentence to emphasize that what follows goes against the speaker's expectations, while なんて appears at the end of a sentence or phrase to express the same. Because they fill different roles, they are often used together. For example, まさか勝てるなんて！ ('To think we could win!' / 'I never thought we could win').

first_relatable.title: まさか
first_relatable.meaning: I never dreamed, Never, No way, Don't tell me, You don't say
